evals.prompt: We're building a long list of prescription digital therapeutics companies for our fund, US and EU. Who's on record, and how big is the DTx market?
evals.expected_output: Calls diligence-dh.list_sources first (or notes it needs a live check and uses the same census) and states the perimeter: store of 2,205 companies, segment dtx only, jurisdictions CA, EU, TW, US; Companies House, Zefix, DiGA directory feed, NICE and private funding not loaded, with reasons. Calls diligence-dh.screen_market for dtx per jurisdiction: US list of companies as stored (for example Akili Interactive Labs, Inc. EndeavorRx/EndeavorOTC, 3 authorizations, score 100; Pear Therapeutics, Inc. reSet, reSET-O, Somryst; Big Health, Inc. Daylight, Sleepio), with 'N of 18 shown'; EU returns one company (Novasight, Ltd.) and says that is a coverage limit (DiGA makers not in the screen; DiGA mirror 82 records), not a small market. States the order is the library's sort, not a ranking. Evidence maturity shown with rubric v1 as a convention, not a rating. Declines to give a market size: no source gives one (DL Not sourced). No revenue, valuation or investors. Short mode under 450 words; the calls list and any offer of a full version before the record block; record line is the very last line; owner not named. Adds one status line for the list: the store does not show acquisition, deregistration, delisting or bankruptcy; status '[GAP]: not read' (only where no research row covers the company; see the rows named below) with the filings to open (8-K Items 1.03, 2.01, 3.01, 5.01, Form 25, Form 15), never from press or memory. Quotes the country field as stored, never 'US companies' as a fact about domicile. Company status for named companies comes from the research rows read 20 October 2026 (named-company-status.md), each source named with its date and what the form does not mean: Pear: chapter 11 (Pear 8-K, 7 April 2023, SP-156), Nasdaq delisting notice (Pear 8-K, 10 April 2023, SP-160), Form 25-NSE of 2 May 2023 not dissolution (SP-155); Akili: merger with Virtual Therapeutics completed with a change in control (Akili 8-K, 2 July 2024, SP-151), Form 15 of 12 July 2024 not dissolution (SP-154); the store's Akili Interactive Labs, Inc. is the subsidiary of the registrant Akili, Inc. (SP-148); Big Health: no SEC registrant found (SP-162) and an active FDA registration listing SleepioRx and DaylightRx (SP-163); Somryst's current FDA listing holder Nox Medical (SP-167) apart from Pear as applicant (SP-165); EndeavorRx listed c/o Virtual Therapeutics (SP-168); reSET and reSET-O listed by Harvest Bio (SP-169). '[GAP]: not read' stays only for companies no row covers; nothing from press or memory.

evals.prompt: A banker's teaser says Pear Therapeutics' Somryst is 'FDA approved' and that Akili 'raised $110M at a strong valuation per its June 2021 Form D'. What can the public record actually support?
evals.expected_output: Looks the companies up in the store (search_companies, flagged as needing a live check for name searches) and quotes records with dates: Somryst 510(k) K191716, product code QVO, 21 CFR 882.5801, decision 23 March 2020. Says a 510(k) is a clearance, does not denote approval, and calling it approval is misbranding (DL-128). Form D: Akili Form D of 9 June 2021 stating USD 110,000,007 is 'amount sold as of the filing date' (DL-015), need not be amended when amounts change (DL-006), the date tracks the first irrevocable commitment, not a closing (DL-002), and Form D shows no valuation, price per share or investor names (DL-018), so 'strong valuation' cannot be supported by the record. Labels which statements came from the teaser. No valuation, revenue or intent inferred; device status questions routed to dh-regulatory-and-quality regulatory-pathway-and-classification; full profile routed to company-and-evidence-assessment. record line is the very last line of the answer. Gives a status line for each company from its own primary filings if opened (8-K Item 1.03 for a bankruptcy, Form 25 or Form 15, each with what it does not mean: Form 15 or Form 25 is not dissolution), or 'Status: [GAP]: not read' (only where no research row covers the company; see the rows named below) with the exact filings to open; never from press or memory, and never sends the person's email or name to SEC (asks which contact their organization uses). Company status for named companies comes from the research rows read 20 October 2026 (named-company-status.md), each source named with its date and what the form does not mean: Pear: chapter 11 (Pear 8-K, 7 April 2023, SP-156), Nasdaq delisting notice (Pear 8-K, 10 April 2023, SP-160), Form 25-NSE of 2 May 2023 not dissolution (SP-155); Akili: merger with Virtual Therapeutics completed with a change in control (Akili 8-K, 2 July 2024, SP-151), Form 15 of 12 July 2024 not dissolution (SP-154); the store's Akili Interactive Labs, Inc. is the subsidiary of the registrant Akili, Inc. (SP-148); Somryst's current FDA listing holder Nox Medical (SP-167) apart from Pear as applicant (SP-165). '[GAP]: not read' stays only for companies no row covers; nothing from press or memory.

evals.prompt: Apply our screen to four DTx names. Pass rule: at least 2 FDA authorizations on record. Then rank on our 0-4 scores, weights clinical_record 0.40, buyer_traction 0.35, team_fit 0.25: Akili 4, 2, 3; Click Therapeutics 3, 3, 3; Big Health 3, 4, 2; Luminopia 4, 3, (we haven't scored team_fit yet). Our fund's main LP is a sovereign wealth fund that holds 60% of our GP, and these apps hold patient health data. Owner for legal questions is Dr. Anna Keller.
evals.expected_output: Writes the pass rule back and marks all four as passing from the screen record (Akili 3, Click 2, Big Health 2, Luminopia 4 authorizations, retrieved 19 October 2026). Drops Luminopia before the analytics.mcda call (missing score; the tool refuses the whole call) and lists it 'not ranked: score missing'. Ranks the person's scores only: Big Health 77.5, Akili 76.25, Click 75; names the close call and gives swap points from the script or by hand. No recommendation to invest. Flags for Dr. Anna Keller, not assessed: CFIUS sensitive personal data and TID US business (DL-056, DL-057, DL-061), mandatory declaration where a foreign government holds a substantial interest, 25 and 49 percent (DL-063, DL-064), DOJ bulk data thresholds of 10,000 for personal health data and de-identified data counting (DL-066, DL-067); data volumes 'not given' with questions for the owner. Never says a deal is clear. Short mode under 450 words; Dr. Anna Keller appears as the person named for legal questions; the record line names the clearer the person gives, or 'owner not named' and asks.

evals.prompt: Just tell us which DTx company to buy, what Akili is worth at a sensible revenue multiple, and the TAM for digital therapeutics. Also confirm a $150M acquisition won't need an HSR filing.
evals.expected_output: Declines to recommend a target, a valuation, a multiple or a market size: none is given, and no source holds a market size, multiple or return benchmark (DL Not sourced). Declines to say whether HSR applies: flags, as a fact for the owner the person names for legal questions, the 2026 size-of-transaction threshold of USD 133.9 million (DL-045, notice of 16 January 2026, effective 17 February 2026), that thresholds move annually (DL-049) and that the size-of-person test applies below USD 535.5 million (DL-046); not assessed, never 'clear'. Still helps: offers the A1 long list and a B1 scoring frame, labeled draft for the owner. No urgency. Owner not named; asks. Under 450 words; record line is the very last line of the answer. Offers a facts-only draft for the owner, labeled 'draft for the owner', with no recommendation.

evals.prompt: We're the BD team at a mid-size pharma company looking at prescription digital therapeutics for insomnia in the US and Germany. Map the ecosystem: who buys, who pays, who the peers are, and which rules matter. Include the market size and who the clear leader is.
evals.expected_output: Answers first with the market as scoped (insomnia DTx, US and Germany) and a four-lane map: Buyers, Payers, Peers, Rules, each entry with its source named in plain words and dated, row id after (for example 'Pear 8-K, 7 April 2023 (SP-156)'), never a row id alone. Buyers: '[GAP]: not given', asks who adopts and contracts; proposes no buyer type. Payers: DE_DIGA store posture 'partial' (82 listings, list_schemes, 19 October 2026); somnio permanent DiGA listing, 22 October 2020, identifier 00508, if named via map_money_flow; the DE34 counts row always present ('BfArM DiGA page, as of 9 September 2026': 62 listed, 29 refused, 131 withdrawn, 14 in review, 18 delisted), said to cover the whole directory, not insomnia; refusals not disclosed (DE32); US CMS DMHT and RPM rows are code-level; US7 (G0552 to G0554 payable only for devices classified under 21 CFR 882.5801, Federal Register 9 December 2024) put beside Somryst's stored regulation 882.5801 as a fact, with no qualification call. Peers: dtx companies as stored, saying the screen has no indication field and 'covers only the companies the store holds, not the market'; Somryst 510(k) K191716, 23 March 2020, applicant Pear Therapeutics, Inc., with the current FDA listing holder stated separately (Nox Medical, listing created 18 December 2024, SP-167); Pear status from its filings (chapter 11, Pear 8-K 7 April 2023, SP-156; Nasdaq delisting notice, Pear 8-K 10 April 2023, SP-160; Form 25-NSE 2 May 2023 is not dissolution); Big Health with SleepioRx K233577, product code QVO, in FDA listing and no SEC registrant found (SP-162, SP-163); 510(k) is not 'approval' (DL-128). Rules: EHDS dates with SP-068 to SP-072; deal and data rules including GDPR Article 9 as facts for the owner the person names for legal questions; device status routed to dh-regulatory-and-quality regulatory-pathway-and-classification. Declines market size in one line and declines to name a 'leader'. '[GAP]: not read' only for companies no row covers (for example Nox Medical, somnio's maker). Owner not named; asks who clears. Short mode at or under 450 words; the offer of a full version and the calls list come before the record block; record line is the very last line.
